_doc: Cloudflare edge rate limiting rules, declared here so they are reviewable
in the repo rather than living only in a dashboard (M3 task 3.2e).
WHY THE EDGE AND NOT OUR CODE. Per-source limiting needs the client IP.
Cloudflare already handles it as a matter of routing on every request
whether or not we act on it, so a rule here leaves CUSTODY of network
identity where it already sits. Keying our own counters on an IP, or on a
hash or any other derivative, moves custody to MarginSheet and is refused:
the bright line is the value, not its reversibility. Ruled by Guy,
16 Aug 2026. See the network identity doctrine in CLAUDE.md.
WHY IT IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE. A control living only in the Cloudflare
dashboard is exactly what broke production deploys on 16 Aug 2026: the
api.marginsheet.com route existed only in the UI until a PR moved it into
the repo. The edge-rules CI job reads the live ruleset and fails if a rule
declared here is absent or altered, so drift is a red build rather than a
discovery.
THESE VALUES ARE THE FREE TIER'S FIXED SHAPE, NOT A CHOICE (16 Aug 2026).
The rule was designed as 10 requests per 60 seconds keyed on ip.src plus
cf.colo.id, with a 10 minute mitigation. Cloudflare's free plan does not
offer any of that: the period is fixed at 10 seconds and not adjustable,
the characteristics dropdown is inert and allows IP only, and the
mitigation timeout is not exposed. What is declared below is what the
platform permits, deployed at those values with a block action.
WHAT A PAID PLAN WOULD CHANGE, so whoever upgrades knows to revisit this:
period              10 -> 60 seconds
characteristics     add cf.colo.id as a second characteristic, so the
counter is per data centre and a distributed source
cannot spread its budget across colos
mitigation_timeout  becomes settable; 600 seconds was the intent
WHAT THIS COSTS TODAY, stated rather than implied. Ten requests per ten
seconds is a burst brake, not a sustained-rate control: a patient attacker
stays under it indefinitely. That makes the two limits in our own code
load-bearing rather than secondary. The global ceiling in particular is now
the binding cost control, since production allows 500 sends an hour and
this rule alone would permit far more. Recorded so nobody reads the
presence of an edge rule as covering the spray case fully.
mitigation_timeout is deliberately absent from the comparison below: the
free plan does not expose it, so there is no setting that could drift. It
returns to the declaration on upgrade, along with the values above.
zone_id is not a secret; it appears in every wrangler deploy log.

rules.why: Spray across many addresses from one source. Per-email limiting caps how often ONE address is mailed and does nothing about an attacker walking a list, which is the attack this covers.
